**AI 380: Human-AI Interaction · Willamette University**

**Running example:** `Calm_Wordle`, an accessible Wordle game with an optional Rasa assistant.

**Outcome:** The project runs in Docker, lives in GitHub, and is reachable from any phone or laptop at `https://<your-name>.<region>.cloudapp.azure.com`.

## 🛠️ How to use this workshop

1. Read the concept.
2. Run the command or edit the named file.
3. Pass the checkpoint.
4. Continue only when it passes.

::: {.checkpoint}
**Budget:** Use a free or student-credit Azure VM. Set a budget alert before creating anything (Part 4).
:::

## ✅ Five things you will do

1. 🐳 Package the project in a Docker image.
2. 🧪 Test the container on your own machine.
3. 🐙 Put the project in a GitHub repo.
4. ☁️ Create a free Azure VM and open the web ports.
5. 🚀 Pull the repo onto the VM and start it with automatic HTTPS.

## 🔒 Why HTTPS is not optional

Browsers only allow the **microphone** (speech recognition) on `https://` pages or on `localhost`.

A deployed voice app on plain `http://` **silently loses its microphone**.

> The setup below gets a free certificate automatically.

## 📦 What actually gets deployed

| Piece | In the Docker image? | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `web_server.py`, `web/` | ✅ Yes | The game page and its JSON API |
| `actions/` game logic | ✅ Yes | Rules, hints, voice-command parser |
| Rasa server, trained `models/` | ❌ No | Needs a license and far more memory (Part 10) |

The live site is the **visual and voice-command game**. The Rasa chat and voice assistant is a separate, optional deployment.

## 📋 Prerequisites

- A working project folder (`Calm_Wordle`) that runs locally.
- [Docker Desktop](https://www.docker.com/products/docker-desktop/) installed and running.
- [GitHub Desktop](https://desktop.github.com/) and a GitHub account.
- An Azure account (Part 4).
- A terminal: **PowerShell** on Windows, **Terminal** on macOS.

## ① Containerize and secure {.section-slide background-color="#0067b8"}

::: {.eyebrow}
Parts 1–3 · Docker, Compose, GitHub
:::

**Image → container → HTTPS proxy → repo**

## 🐳 Part 1 · Containerize the project

**Vocabulary**

- **Dockerfile:** a recipe for building an image.
- **Image:** a frozen copy of your app plus everything it needs.
- **Container:** a running image.

## 📄 1.1 · Read the Dockerfile

**`Calm_Wordle/Dockerfile`**

```dockerfile
FROM python:3.12-slim

WORKDIR /app
COPY actions/__init__.py actions/english.py actions/answers.py \
     actions/wordle_logic.py actions/game.py actions/voice_commands.py actions/
COPY web/ web/
COPY web_server.py .

RUN useradd --create-home player && mkdir /data && chown player /data
USER player

ENV HOST=0.0.0.0 PORT=8000 SAVE_FILE=/data/saved_games.json
EXPOSE 8000
CMD ["python", "web_server.py"]
```

::: {.notes}
In the actual file the COPY of actions/ files is on one line; it is wrapped here to fit the slide.
:::

## 🔍 Line by line

| Line | Why |
|---|---|
| `FROM python:3.12-slim` | Small official Python base image |
| `COPY ...` | Only the files the game needs. No models, no virtual environment, no saved games |
| `useradd` / `USER player` | Runs as a normal user, not root. Safer if compromised |
| `HOST=0.0.0.0` | Listen on all interfaces so outside traffic can reach the container |
| `SAVE_FILE=/data/...` | Saved games go to `/data`, mounted as a persistent volume |

## ▶️ 1.2 · Build and run

From the `Calm_Wordle` folder:

```bash
docker build -t calm-wordle .
docker run --rm -p 8000:8000 calm-wordle
```

Open <http://localhost:8000>. If the game loads, containerization worked. Stop with `Ctrl+C`.

## 💾 1.3 · Keep saved games

A container's filesystem is deleted when the container is removed. A **volume** survives:

```bash
docker run --rm -p 8000:8000 -v games:/data calm-wordle
```

::: {.checkpoint}
**Checkpoint 1:** `docker build` finishes without errors, and <http://localhost:8000> shows the game.
:::

## 🔐 Part 2 · HTTPS with Docker Compose

**Docker Compose** runs several containers together from one file.

We need two:

- **The game**
- **Caddy:** a web server that fetches and renews HTTPS certificates by itself

## 🧱 2.1 · `deploy/docker-compose.yml`

```yaml
services:
  game:
    build: ..
    restart: unless-stopped
    volumes:
      - games:/data

  caddy:
    image: caddy:2
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "80:80"
      - "443:443"
    environment:
      DOMAIN: ${DOMAIN}
    volumes:
      - ./Caddyfile:/etc/caddy/Caddyfile:ro
      - caddy_data:/data
    depends_on:
      - game

volumes:
  games:
  caddy_data:
```

## 📝 2.2 · `deploy/Caddyfile`

```text
{$DOMAIN} {
	encode gzip
	reverse_proxy game:8000
}
```

For the site name in `DOMAIN`: get a certificate, then forward requests to the `game` container on port 8000.

## 💡 Key ideas in the Compose file

- **Only Caddy** publishes ports to the internet; the game is reachable only through Caddy.
- `restart: unless-stopped` brings both containers back after a VM reboot.
- `caddy_data` stores the certificates. Without it, every restart requests new ones and you may hit **rate limits**.

## 🧪 2.3 · Test locally (optional)

Caddy treats `localhost` specially and makes its own local certificate:

```bash
cd deploy
DOMAIN=localhost docker compose up --build
```

Open <https://localhost> and accept the browser warning.

Stop with `Ctrl+C`, then run `docker compose down`.

## 🐙 Part 3 · `.gitignore` first

In the `Calm_Wordle` folder, create `.gitignore`:

```text
.DS_Store
__pycache__/
*.pyc
.venv/
.rasa/
models/
saved_games.json
.env
```

Keeps junk, large folders, **player data and secrets** out of the repo.

## 🖥️ 3.1 · Create the repo with GitHub Desktop

1. **File → Add Local Repository…** and pick `Calm_Wordle`. If it says "not a Git repository," click **create a repository**.
2. In **Changes**, you must see `Dockerfile`, `web_server.py`, `web/`, `actions/`, `deploy/`, `.gitignore`. You must **not** see `models/`, `.rasa/`, `saved_games.json`.
3. Summary: `Initial commit` → **Commit to main**.
4. **Publish repository** (choose private if you prefer).

> The repo root must be `Calm_Wordle` itself, because `docker-compose.yml` uses `build: ..`.

## 🔄 3.2 · The update loop

You will use this for the rest of the course.

1. Edit a file and save.
2. In GitHub Desktop, write a summary and click **Commit to main**.
3. Click **Push origin**.

An empty **Changes** list means nothing changed since the last commit. That is normal.

::: {.checkpoint}
**Checkpoint 3:** The repo appears on github.com, contains `Dockerfile` and `deploy/`, and does **not** contain `models/` or `.env`.
:::

## ② Build the server {.section-slide background-color="#263b4e"}

::: {.eyebrow}
Parts 4–6 · Azure account, VM, Docker
:::

**Budget → VM → open ports → Docker**

## 🎓 Part 4 · Free Azure credit

Pick one option.

| Option | What you get | Needs |
|---|---|---|
| **Azure for Students** | About $100 credit and free services for 12 months; no credit card | A school email address |
| **Azure free account** | 12 months of free services, a monthly allowance of small Linux VM hours, plus a starter credit | A credit or debit card for identity check |

- <https://azure.microsoft.com/free/students>
- <https://azure.microsoft.com/free>

## 🔎 Check the offer before you start

Offers change. Look for the **B1s** Linux VM in the free services list. If your region lists a different size, use that one.

Any small Linux VM with **at least 1 GB RAM** works for the game.

## 💸 Protect yourself from surprise charges

1. Portal: **Cost Management + Billing → Budgets**. Create a **$5 budget** with an email alert.
2. A VM stopped from the operating system (`shutdown`) **still bills**. Use **deallocate** (Part 9).

::: {.checkpoint}
**Checkpoint 4:** Account created and budget alert exists.
:::

## 🖥️ Part 5 · Create the VM

The CLI is faster and repeatable than portal clicks. Use **Azure Cloud Shell**: no installation.

1. Sign in to <https://portal.azure.com>.
2. Click the `>_` icon in the top bar and choose **Bash**.
3. Accept the storage prompt if it appears.

## 🏷️ 5.1 · Pick unique names

Replace `yourname` with lowercase letters and numbers. The DNS label must be unique across the whole Azure region.

```bash
RG=calmwordle-rg
VM=calmwordle-vm
LOC=westus2
DNS=calmwordle-yourname
```

`westus2` is close to Oregon. If the size is unavailable, try `westus3`, `eastus`, or `centralus`.

## 🧰 5.2 · Resource group and VM

A **resource group** is a folder for related resources. Deleting it removes everything inside.

```bash
az group create --name $RG --location $LOC

az vm create \
  --resource-group $RG \
  --name $VM \
  --image Ubuntu2404 \
  --size Standard_B1s \
  --admin-username azureuser \
  --generate-ssh-keys \
  --public-ip-sku Standard \
  --public-ip-address-dns-name $DNS
```

## 📝 Notes on `az vm create`

- `--generate-ssh-keys` creates a key pair if you have none. You log in with the **key**, not a password.
- The command prints JSON. Look for `publicIpAddress`.
- If you get `The requested VM size is not available`, list sizes and rerun with `--size`:

```bash
az vm list-skus --location $LOC --size Standard_B1 --output table
```

## 🔓 5.3 · Open the web ports

SSH (22) is open by default. Web traffic needs **80** and **443**. Port 80 is required for the certificate check.

```bash
az vm open-port --resource-group $RG --name $VM --port 80  --priority 900
az vm open-port --resource-group $RG --name $VM --port 443 --priority 901
```

## 🌐 5.4 · Get your site address

```bash
az vm show -d --resource-group $RG --name $VM --query fqdns -o tsv
```

Result looks like `calmwordle-yourname.westus2.cloudapp.azure.com`. **Write it down.**

If empty, build it yourself: `$DNS.$LOC.cloudapp.azure.com`.

::: {.checkpoint}
**Checkpoint 5:** You have a public IP and a `*.cloudapp.azure.com` name.
:::

## 🔑 Part 6 · Prepare the server

### 6.1 · Log in

From Cloud Shell:

```bash
ssh azureuser@$DNS.$LOC.cloudapp.azure.com
```

Type `yes` to trust the host. The prompt becomes `azureuser@calmwordle-vm`.

From your own laptop instead: copy the private key from Cloud Shell, or create a key on your laptop and pass it with `--ssh-key-values`.

## 🐳 6.2 · Install Docker

```bash
sudo apt-get update
curl -fsSL https://get.docker.com | sudo sh
sudo usermod -aG docker $USER
exit
```

**Log in again** so the new group membership applies, then check:

```bash
docker --version
docker compose version
```

::: {.checkpoint}
**Checkpoint 6:** Both commands print a version and `docker ps` runs without `sudo`.
:::

## ③ Deploy and operate {.section-slide background-color="#a93632"}

::: {.eyebrow}
Parts 7–9 · Code, HTTPS launch, clean-up
:::

**Clone → launch → verify → update → deallocate**

## 📥 Part 7 · Get your code onto the VM

### 7.1 · Public repo

```bash
cd ~
git clone https://github.com/YOUR_GITHUB_USER/Calm_Wordle.git calm-wordle
```

Use your real username and repo name. The repo name is **case-sensitive** in the URL.

Find them in GitHub Desktop: **Repository → Repository settings → Remote**.

## 🗝️ 7.2 · Private repo: deploy key

A **deploy key** gives this one VM **read-only** access to this one repo.

On the VM:

```bash
ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "azure-vm" -f ~/.ssh/deploy_key -N ""
cat ~/.ssh/deploy_key.pub
```

On GitHub: repo **Settings → Deploy keys → Add deploy key**. Paste the line, leave **Allow write access unchecked**, save.

## 🗝️ Deploy key · Tell SSH to use it

Back on the VM:

```bash
cat >> ~/.ssh/config <<'EOF'
Host github.com
  IdentityFile ~/.ssh/deploy_key
  IdentitiesOnly yes
EOF
chmod 600 ~/.ssh/config
ssh -T git@github.com
```

Expect: `Hi USER/REPO! You've successfully authenticated`. Then:

```bash
cd ~
git clone git@github.com:YOUR_GITHUB_USER/Calm_Wordle.git calm-wordle
```

## ⚠️ Common clone mistakes

| Message | Cause |
|---|---|
| `Authentication failed` over HTTPS | Repo is private. GitHub rejects account passwords for Git. Use the deploy key |
| `Repository not found` | Wrong username or repo name, or key added to a different repo |
| Literal `YOUR_GITHUB_USER` | Replace placeholders with your real values |

## 🚀 Part 8 · Launch with HTTPS

On the VM:

```bash
cd ~/calm-wordle/deploy
echo "DOMAIN=calmwordle-yourname.westus2.cloudapp.azure.com" > .env
docker compose up -d --build
docker compose ps
docker compose logs -f caddy
```

Use the exact name from step 5.4. Compose reads `.env` in the same folder automatically.

## 👀 Watch the certificate arrive

- After about a minute, the Caddy log shows the certificate was obtained.
- Press `Ctrl+C` to stop reading logs. **The containers keep running.**
- Open `https://calmwordle-yourname.westus2.cloudapp.azure.com` on your laptop **and phone**.
- Test the microphone.

## 🩺 Test from the command line

Use GET. `curl -I` sends HEAD, which this small server does not implement: it returns **501** even when everything works.

```bash
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" \
  https://calmwordle-yourname.westus2.cloudapp.azure.com/
```

Expected output: `200`

::: {.checkpoint}
**Checkpoint 8:** The `https://` site loads on a laptop and a phone, and the microphone works.
:::

## 🔄 Deploy an update

On your laptop: edit, commit, **Push origin**. Then on the VM:

```bash
cd ~/calm-wordle && git pull && cd deploy && docker compose up -d --build
```

Saved games live in the `games` volume, so they **survive rebuilds**.

## 🧯 Troubleshooting · Network and certificate

| Symptom | Likely cause → Fix |
|---|---|
| Browser cannot connect | Ports 80/443 not open → rerun the two `az vm open-port` commands |
| Certificate invalid or connection reset | Not issued yet → `docker compose logs caddy`, wait a minute |
| `could not get certificate`, `timeout` | Port 80 blocked or wrong `DOMAIN` → `cat .env`; check NSG rules under VM, Networking |
| Rate limit in the log | Many students share the Azure domain suffix → Caddy falls back to a second provider; wait |

## 🧯 Troubleshooting · Docker and browser

| Symptom | Likely cause → Fix |
|---|---|
| `permission denied` running `docker` | No re-login after `usermod` → `exit`, log in again |
| `variable DOMAIN is not set` | No `.env` in `deploy/` → recreate it (Part 8) |
| Microphone blocked | Page is on `http://` → use `https://` |
| `port is already allocated` | Another service uses 80/443 → run `sudo ss -tlnp` and look for `:80` and `:443` |
| Build runs out of memory | Very small VM → add swap (next slide) |

## 🧯 Add swap on a tiny VM

```bash
sudo fallocate -l 1G /swapfile
sudo chmod 600 /swapfile
sudo mkswap /swapfile
sudo swapon /swapfile
```

## 🛑 Part 9 · Stop, restart, clean up

Azure bills for compute while a VM is **allocated**, even when the OS is shut down. Deallocate from the CLI:

```bash
az vm deallocate --resource-group calmwordle-rg --name calmwordle-vm
az vm start      --resource-group calmwordle-rg --name calmwordle-vm
```

- Public IP and DNS name stay the same with a Standard SKU IP.
- Containers with `restart: unless-stopped` start by themselves.

## 🗑️ Delete everything

When the course is over, one command removes it all:

```bash
az group delete --name calmwordle-rg --yes
```

::: {.checkpoint}
**Checkpoint 9:** You can deallocate and restart the VM, and you know how to delete the resource group.
:::

## 🤖 Part 10 (optional) · Deploy Rasa itself

The live site does **not** run Rasa. To run the assistant on a VM:

1. Use the compose file from the Lab 4 template (official `rasa/rasa-pro` image, project folder mounted).
2. Put `RASA_LICENSE` and API keys in `.env` on the VM. **Never commit `.env`.**
3. Train on the VM or copy a model in. The image is large and needs **well over 1 GB RAM**; use a 4 GB VM, which uses credit and is not in the free allowance.

## 🤖 Rasa · Security and wiring

4. **Do not publish port 5005** to the internet. Keep it on localhost behind Caddy, or restrict it to your IP in the Azure network rules. An open Rasa API lets anyone spend your LLM keys.
5. In `credentials.yml`, keep secrets in environment variables.

> `web/voice.html` expects Rasa on port 5005 with the `websockets_voice` channel. Check `credentials.yml` and `endpoints.yml` before going online.

## 🌍 Part 11 (optional) · Your own domain

1. Keep the VM's public IP: `az vm show -d ... --query publicIps -o tsv`
2. At your DNS provider, add an **A record**: host `calmwordle`, value `<the VM IP>`.
3. Wait for DNS: `dig +short calmwordle.yourdomain.com` should print the IP.
4. Change `DOMAIN` in `deploy/.env`, then run `docker compose up -d`.

## 🌍 Own domain · Another site on 80/443?

If nginx (or similar) already uses ports 80 and 443, **do not start Caddy**. Publish the game on `127.0.0.1:8100`, proxy to it, and use certbot.

**`deploy/docker-compose.override.yml`**

```yaml
services:
  game:
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:8100:8000"
  caddy:
    profiles: ["disabled"]
```

Then run `docker compose up -d --build game`.

## 🛡️ Security checklist

- [ ] SSH uses a key, not a password
- [ ] Only ports 22, 80, and 443 are open in the network security group
- [ ] `.env`, `models/`, and `saved_games.json` are not in the repo
- [ ] The app runs as a non-root user in the container
- [ ] The Rasa API port is not open to the internet
- [ ] A budget alert exists in Cost Management

## 📇 Command cheat sheet · Local

| Task | Command |
|---|---|
| Build image | `docker build -t calm-wordle .` |
| Run locally | `docker run --rm -p 8000:8000 -v games:/data calm-wordle` |
| Status | `docker compose ps` |
| Logs | `docker compose logs -f game` (or `caddy`) |
| Stop | `docker compose down` |

## 📇 Command cheat sheet · Server and Azure

| Task | Command |
|---|---|
| Start on server | `cd ~/calm-wordle/deploy && docker compose up -d --build` |
| Update | `cd ~/calm-wordle && git pull && cd deploy && docker compose up -d --build` |
| Deallocate VM | `az vm deallocate -g calmwordle-rg -n calmwordle-vm` |
| Delete everything | `az group delete -n calmwordle-rg --yes` |

Submit:

1. The GitHub repo URL.
2. Your live `https://` URL.
3. A screenshot of the game running on your phone.
4. A short note: **one thing that went wrong and how you fixed it.**

> A deployed project is one you can update, secure, and shut down.
